tools.description:
- Efficiently explores file system structure
- Supports recursive listing with depth control
- Default ignores common build/cache directories: .git, .venv, node_modules, __pycache__, .mypy_cache, dist, build, etc.
- Pass ignore_patterns to add extra exclusions, or leave empty to use defaults only
- Returns metadata like size, modification time, and type
- Results are limited to 50 items by default; set limit to get more. If truncated=true, narrow your query
- Use this tool when you need to understand the directory structure or find files in a specific path

depth.description: The maximum recursion depth. 0 means current directory only. Defaults to 0.

dir_path.description: The path to the directory to list.

ignore_patterns.description: Optional: Custom glob patterns to ignore (e.g., ['*.tmp', 'node_modules']).

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. Defaults to 50. Increase if results are truncated.

recursive.description: Whether to list subdirectories recursively. Defaults to false.

tools.name: list_dir

tools.description:
- Reads and returns the content of a specified file
- Supports line-based slicing for reading specific portions of large files
- Full reads of files larger than 25KB are truncated to the first ~1KB of content and marked with 'truncated: true' (plus a notice); use 'start_line'/'end_line' or 'grep_search' to page through large files
- Detects and rejects binary files for safety
- Each content line is prefixed with its 1-based line number (e.g. "   12│code") for reference
- When using 'edit', provide the exact text WITHOUT the line-number prefix
- Use this tool when you need to read the contents of a file to understand its logic or data

encoding.description: Optional: The file encoding to use. Defaults to utf-8.

end_line.description: Optional: The 1-based line number to end reading at (inclusive). Defaults to the end of the file or 500 lines.

file_path.description: The path to the file to read.

start_line.description: Optional: The 1-based line number to start reading from. Defaults to 1.

tools.name: read_file

tools.description:
- Reads and returns an image file as base64 plus metadata (mime_type/format/width/height/size_bytes)
- Detects format by magic bytes (png/jpeg/gif/webp/bmp), not by file extension
- Width/height are returned for png/jpeg/gif; webp/bmp return 0 (no external image lib in v1)
- Rejects images over the max size limit (default 5MB; 0 disables the limit)
- Use this tool when the agent needs to view or analyze an image file (e.g. a screenshot)

file_path.description: The path to the image file to read.

tools.name: read_image

tools.description:
- Writes complete content to a specified file
- Automatically creates missing parent directories
- Uses atomic writing (temp file then rename) for safety
- Enforces a size limit to prevent accidental large writes
- Use this tool when you need to create a new file or fully overwrite an existing one

content.description: The complete content to write. Provide the full file; do not use placeholders.

encoding.description: Optional: The file encoding to use. Defaults to utf-8.

file_path.description: The path to the file to write.

tools.name: write_file

tools.description:
- Performs precision string replacement in a file
- Requires an exact, unique match for the 'old_string' unless 'allow_multiple' is set
- Preserves indentation and line endings
- Use this tool when you need to make surgical changes to specific parts of a file without rewriting it entirely

allow_multiple.description: Optional: If true, replace all occurrences of 'old_string'. Defaults to false.

file_path.description: The path to the file to modify.

instruction.description: Optional: A brief description of the change.

new_string.description: The exact literal text to replace 'old_string' with.

old_string.description: The exact literal text to replace. Must match exactly including whitespace.

tools.name: edit

tools.description:
- High-performance code searching tool
- Supports both literal strings and regular expressions
- Provides context lines around matches to help understand code logic
- Includes built-in safety limits for total matches and matches per file
- Use this tool when you need to find specific strings, patterns, or definitions across multiple files without reading them one by one
- NOTE: Common build, dependency, and version control directories (e.g., .git, node_modules, dist, build, .venv) and binary/media file types are automatically excluded to improve performance and reduce noise.

case_sensitive.description: Optional: Whether the search should be case-sensitive. Defaults to false.

context.description: Optional: Number of context lines to return around each match.

exclude_pattern.description: Optional: Glob pattern to exclude files or paths.

fixed_strings.description: Optional: If true, treat the pattern as a literal string. Defaults to false (regex).

include_pattern.description: Optional: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g., '*.go').

max_matches_per_file.description: Optional: Maximum matches to return per individual file. Defaults to 10.

path.description: Optional: Subdirectory to search within. Defaults to the current directory.

pattern.description: The regex or literal pattern to search for.

total_max_matches.description: Optional: Maximum total matches to return across all files. Defaults to 100.

tools.name: grep_search

tools.description:
- Fast file pattern matching tool that works with any codebase size
- Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts"
- Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time
- Use this tool when you need to find files by name patterns
- When you are doing an open ended search that may require multiple rounds of globbing and grepping, use the Agent tool instead
- You can call multiple tools in a single response. It is always better to speculatively perform multiple searches in parallel if they are potentially useful.

case_sensitive.description: Optional: Whether the glob search should be case-sensitive. Defaults to false.

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match against (e.g., 'src/**/*.go').

tools.name: glob

tools.description:
- Executes a shell command in a controlled environment
- Shell: Unix: commands are interpreted by `bash -c`
- Paths: Working directory: the directory gtsp was started from, or --workdir if given (execute_bash does not change it per call).
Paths: ordinary POSIX paths, the same ones read_file/write_file use.
- Three execution modes:
  1. Synchronous with timeout (default): command runs up to task_timeout seconds (default 180s); if still running, the action taken depends on 'timeout_action'
  2. Synchronous no timeout: use run_in_background:true to start immediately in background
  3. Background (run_in_background:true): starts immediately in background, returns process_id right away
- Use process_output to poll or wait for background process completion
- Automatically truncates large outputs to protect context window
- Use this tool when you need to run shell commands, build scripts, run tests, or perform other system-level operations

command.description: The exact shell command to execute. Unix: commands are interpreted by `bash -c`.

description.description: Optional: A brief description of the command's purpose.

run_in_background.description: Optional: Start the process immediately in the background and return a process_id right away, without waiting. Unlike setting task_timeout=0 (which falls back to the default 180s and only promotes to background if the command is still running then), this never blocks. Defaults to false.

task_timeout.description: Optional: Timeout in seconds (default 180s). When the command exceeds this timeout, the action taken depends on 'timeout_action'. Set to 0 to use the default timeout.

timeout_action.description: Optional: Action to take when task_timeout expires. 'background' (default) promotes the process to background and returns a process_id. 'kill' terminates the process and returns partial output.

tools.name: execute_bash

tools.description:
- Retrieves output from a running or completed background process
- Use block:true (default) to wait for process completion up to the timeout
- Use block:false for a non-blocking snapshot of current output
- Returns stdout, stderr, running status, and exit code when complete
- Process IDs are only valid while the server session is active; they are lost on server restart
- process_id is only returned when a process is promoted to background (via task_timeout expiry or run_in_background:true), not for processes that complete synchronously

block.description: Whether to wait for process completion. Defaults to true.

process_id.description: The process ID returned by execute_bash.

timeout.description: Max wait time in ms when block:true. Defaults to 30000, max 60000. Note: actual effective wait time is also limited by the client's transport request timeout (typically 30-65s); if you need to wait longer, use block:false and poll repeatedly.

tools.name: process_output

tools.description:
- Terminates a running background process
- If the process has already exited, this is a no-op and returns successfully
- Returns process_id, success (true/false), and exit_code
- Use this to clean up long-running background processes
tools.name: process_stop

tools.description:
- Lists all currently running background processes started by execute_bash
- Returns process_id, command, running_time, and status for each process
- Use this to check what background processes are active before calling process_output or process_stop
tools.name: process_list
